summary: Crook County lookout first built in 1934, rebuilt in 1968 or 1969 as a 60-ft timber tower with an R6 cabin; on private land, not open to the public.

facts.design: R6 Flat Top cabin atop a 60-ft open timber tower (current structure)

access.note: Private land; NHLR says the lookout is not accessible to the public

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (NHLR lists Ochoco Timber Company as cooperator)

events.note: First wooden tower and cabin; a 1934 newspaper gives 66 ft, firelookout.com gives a 50-ft pole tower
Gordon McNely and his wife took charge in July 1934; before this the fireman was posted at a shearing plant
A teacher's wife and her 12-year-old son manned the station while her husband was at summer school
Seven fires reported during the season; a season count, not a single fire
NHLR dates the replacement tower and cabin to 1968; firelookout.com and the 1969 annual report point to 1969

corrections.proposed: 1968 rebuilt, replacing the 1934 tower and cabin
corrections.why: NHLR says the 1968 tower and cabin replaced the 1934 structures, so 1968 is a rebuild; the record also omits the 1934 original.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR lists Ochoco Timber Company as a cooperator; firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page name the Oregon Department of Forestry for the cab. The record's ODF entry matches the cab.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: 1934 tower height (66 ft in a 1934 newspaper vs 50 ft on firelookout.com). Rebuild year 1968 (NHLR, 1968 report) vs 1969 (firelookout.com, 1969 report); the 1968 and 1969 reports both describe the same winter, so the year depends on how the reports count. Staffing 'every summer' comes from an undated page; the latest dated staffing in the pages read is 1965. No rental information found. Record access 'unknown' can be set to private (NHLR and firelookout.com agree).
